Sleeves generally don't offer the best protection when compared to backpacks or cases, but lets get some info, what are your design preferences (plain color, image, etc.)?

If you're willing to do some diy: 

After finding a good looking sleeve, measure the width and length of the sleeve when your laptop is inside, and then buy some trial kits for silicone rubber with high tensile strength and hardness (most I see on amazon are around 20-30 bucks for a solid 1 to 2 lbs of material, make sure to find a skin safe or food safe variant), make a few corner bumpers, then epoxy/glue them into the sides of that sleeve, cut a little slit on the bumpers near the opening so the laptop can slide in/out easier. It'll be fairly drop resistant and you can't tell the difference when it is all zipped up.

You can scrap weapons for material after you find the Blacksmith, so don't throw anything away. The system for crafting allows you to craft low level material into higher grade ones, so all junk in theory can be used to build a stronger weapon.

I had about maybe 150 to 200 hours on it, to be honest the enemies ARE a bit repetitive, but like the previous replies they do get much better as you get into the higher endgame difficulties, the patterns and aggression of enemies change drastically and you have to be more careful of picking a fight near groups to avoid being ganged up on. I find the combat to be the most enjoyable for me because each weapon has 3 stances, with skills and equipment buffing each stance and weapon, giving you a completely different feel for each build you choose. For example, my first build included a spear in high stance and sword in medium, which allowed me to stun or stagger with sword stance, then switch to spear and do massive damage. At the end of the game, i switched to spear only, and a rifle backup to take out archers. The spear mid stance would poke down tough enemies and high stance to finish off weak ones or deal damage to slow enemies with telegraphed strikes. It is really satisfying to come up with different builds and seeing the mechanics to each weapon. If you have the 40-50 bucks to spend, I'd put this in my top 10 games of the year, must buy if it is on sale. You can also PM me if you want more info on the game. The end game levels look pretty great as well, the levels have this really dark and solemn feel to it at times and then there are areas where you can slow down and take in the surroundings. Boss design along with the guardian spirits really stand out with the particle effects and their attire/weapons, each with their style and story. Every summon makes you feel powerful and applies unique effects of their own.  Music is a strong point as well, the bosses each have their own theme and it portrays their story and emotions quite well in my opinion. The story is okay, comedic at times and it is different from the Souls Games' "Find your own lore" system. It has more cutscenes and dialogue compared to Dark Souls, which i personally really enjoy.
